items.title: Raw TUI honours terminal-overrides, terminal-features and user-keys
accept: With TERM=xterm-256color, no COLORTERM, and `set -as terminal-overrides ',*:Tc'`, the raw TUI emits 24-bit SGR (today it downgrades to 256 at render.rs:3599 while #{client_colours} says 16777216).
terminal-features RGB and extkeys reach the raw TUI from the mask the daemon already computes (daemon.rs:40085-40105); the TUI raises colour depth and arms extended keys from it.
user-keys entries produce User0..User9 keys in the raw TUI and fire `bind UserN` bindings.
options.client-terminal-negotiation keeps only extended-keys-format, assume-paste-time and xterm-keys, with the false 'zz never reads terminfo' claim removed.

items.title: Bytes survive option, environment, command-block and guard-output paths
accept: set -g @x a\376b (argv or source-file -) stores the bytes; show-options -g @x prints a\376b as the pin does, and #{@x} expands to the same bytes as the pin for UTF-8 and non-UTF-8 clients.
A registry item records the divergence first if the store change is split across commits, and closes with it.
Sourcing `if-shell -F 1 { set-buffer -b x a<fe>b }` stores 61 fe 62 as tmux 3.8 does (zz stores 61 ef bf bd 62: command blocks are reparsed through a lossy string view).

X=a<fd>b in one sourced file then set-buffer -b y "$X" in another stores 61 fd 62 as 3.8 does (the second file takes the text-only parse path and reads the lossy global_environment_variable accessor).

A UTF-8 control client gets raw bytes for an inserted or sourced show-buffer as 3.8 does (ControlCommandGuard.output is a String in the protocol today; changing it is a wire append under the unreleased version).
notes: 2026-10-09: found by fix.streams: UserOptions is BTreeMap<String,String> in zz-mux, so non-UTF-8 values read back as U+FFFD; set-option and show-options pass values as String.
2026-10-09: fix.streams handed over its findings 3 and 4 and the guard-output String; measured cases are in protocol.binary-streams' close in compat/tmux-gaps.json.

items.title: Floating panes in the mux and daemon
accept: compat/scenarios/floating-panes.txt matches tmux 3.8 under --strict-geometry, printing list-panes geometry, pane_z, floating, active and modal flags and #{window_layout} after: two new-pane, new-pane with the first of two tiles active, new-pane -t a float, break-pane -W -x 20 -y 6 -X 10 -Y 3, move-pane -P bottom-right, move-pane -L 2, move-pane -z 1, resize-pane -x 30 -y 8 on a float, split-window -h on a float, select-pane of the back float, swap-pane float with tiled, self join-pane, kill of a float, select-layout even-horizontal, resize-window -x 30 -y 10.
In [A, (B / C)], break-pane -W -t A then join-pane -s A -t A restores A beside the whole B/C column with 3.8's geometry.
Every error string in the design's commands table answers verbatim.

Zoom: after resize-pane -Z on a tile, new-pane -A keeps window_zoomed_flag 1 with the float in window_visible_layout; a plain new-pane from that over-zoom float keeps the window zoomed on the new pane; a plain new-pane from a tile unzooms; killing the -A float keeps the zoom; resize-pane -Z on a 20x6 float gives it the window's size and unzoom gives back 20x6; all as 3.8.

Modal: after new-pane -O, select-pane elsewhere keeps it active, break-pane/join-pane/swap-pane answer 'pane is modal', a second -O errors, killing it restores the previous pane, killing the previous pane first makes the close fall back as window_lost_pane does; window_modal_pane and window flag O match 3.8.
select-layout with each window_layout string from the scenario restores the same tree and floats.

No tiled pane: break-pane -W of the sole tile, its kill, and a plain break-pane or join-pane of it into another window each leave a window of floats whose list-panes and window_layout match 3.8; a self join-pane there tiles the float to the whole window; the window closes with its last pane; the snapshot carries LayoutNode::Empty.

Daemon tests: with two attached clients, display-popup -E 'sleep 1' puts one modal in both snapshots, sends no EventPayload::Popup, and closes on exit; from a command client display-popup -E 'exit 3' exits 3; display-popup -C kills a new-pane -O modal; a second display-popup leaves the pane count alone; display-popup "" runs default-command (or the shell) in a live modal, not an empty pane; no u64::MAX pane id remains in crates/zz-daemon/src.
PTY sizes follow the allocation rule (float, zoomed float, hidden float, clamp), and a client size report for a float changes nothing.
A round-trip test pins the appended snapshot, delta, LayoutNode::Empty and MouseKey.press encodings; one move-pane -X emits exactly one TreeOp::WindowLayout.

choose-tree -O z lists panes in pane_z order; pane.floating-model turns adopted with each item closing as proved (option:editor in float.keys, nested-attach-in-popup keeps its fixture requirement); just compat check passes.
notes: 2026-10-09: pin.move moved semantic:move-pane-tiled-extension into adopted pane.floating-model; decide whether it closes or goes back to native.

items.title: Floating panes in the desktop, web/iOS and raw TUI clients
accept: compat/tui-floating.sh matches tmux 3.8 cell for cell: overlapping floats over a vertical split before and after select-pane raises the back one, a -T float under pane-border-status top-floating, pane-border-lines none, display-popup over a zoomed pane, a window with no tiled pane and two floats.
Same fixture: a click on an overlap activates the front float; a click outside a modal does nothing, and kills a new-pane -O -C modal.
A browser pane covered by a float has no kitty placement while covered.

A unit test covers the shared cell-to-pixel rect helper (clipping included) and the drag commit commands: a move sends move-pane -X -Y, a right or bottom edge resize sends resize-pane -x -y, a left, top or top-left corner resize sends resize-pane -x -y ; move-pane -X -Y as one command list whose result is the previewed rectangle; the lane report has desktop and web screenshots of a float, a modal, an over-zoom float and a window with no tiled pane.
A zz-client test shows a focused modal with capture_keys sends the prefix key to the pane.
rg 'PopupState|PopupAction|EventPayload::Popup' finds nothing under crates/zz, crates/zz-tui, crates/zz-client or clients/.

items.title: Move table, prefix * @ g, pane menu Float, mouse drag, editor
accept: list-keys answers 3.8's lines for prefix * @ g Tab BTab and root C-MouseDrag1Pane, C-MouseDrag1Empty, M-MouseDrag1Pane, M-MouseDrag1Border, MouseDown1Control7; list-keys -T move keeps its 19 rows.
Attached TUI: prefix * creates a float, prefix g 1 moves it top-left, prefix @ floats and tiles, pane menu f/t/Move work, with geometry equal to tmux.

compat/tui-mouse.sh, geometry equal to tmux: C-drag from a pane and from empty space creates a float spanning press to pointer (the TUI sends MouseKey.press), M-drag moves, border drag resizes, top-border drag moves, and each gesture's later reports drive the same pane until release; flag:move-pane:-M closes in mouse.bound-context.
With editor set to a script that appends a line, choose-buffer e opens a centred 90% modal and exit 0 updates show-buffer, non-zero leaves it; customize-mode e edits a string option the same way.
keys.move-table closes; keys.default-prefix drops * @ g Tab BTab; option:editor closes.
